coupling reactions using enantioenriched substrates<sup>2−5</sup>
as
well as α-functionalization of prochiral compounds containing

address the inherent challenges associated with the formation

conditions.<sup>9c,12</sup> Nevertheless, despite their synthetic potential,

■ INTRODUCTION

attached to a quaternary stereogenic carbon center represent

accessing these challenging stereocenters.

coupling reactions using enantioenriched substrates<sup>2−5</sup>
as
well as α-functionalization of prochiral compounds containing
azaarene motifs<sup>6,7</sup> have emerged as efective tools. However,
these methodologies often exhibit limitations with respect to
substrate scope, particularly in accommodating diverse
heterocyclic frameworks, and tend to require multistep
preparation of the starting materials or stoichiometric chiral
auxiliaries (Figure 1b, left). In this context, asymmetric
transition metal catalysis has provided a robust platform to
address the inherent challenges associated with the formation
of all-carbon quaternary stereocenters adjacent to nitrogen
atoms. In particular, nickel-catalyzed asymmetric heteroaryla
tion has been reported as a promising strategy for the
stereoselective α-functionalization of azaarenes.<sup>8</sup> Despite its
efectiveness, this approach typically requires high reaction
temperatures and is predominantly limited to substrates with
preassembled cyclic backbones, thereby restricting structural
diversification (Figure 1b, right).

and cost-efective approach to asymmetric catalysis. Recent
advances have showcased the potential of copper-catalyzed
transformations involving π-unsaturated systems�such as

formation of quaternary centers.<sup>11</sup> Allenes, by contrast, have
shown considerable promise in copper-catalyzed coupling
reactions with carbonyl and imine electrophiles, enabling the

conditions.<sup>9c,12</sup> Nevertheless, despite their synthetic potential,

Motivated by these findings, we envisioned a new approach
that would enable the stereoselective construction of α-
quaternary N-heterocycles through copper-catalyzed allene
functionalization. Central to our design is the innate
coordinating ability of the nitrogen atom within the azaarene
ring, which we anticipated could serve to both activate the
substrate and direct the catalytic transformation with high
regio- and stereocontrol. Herein we report the development of
a copper-catalyzed stereoselective synthesis of N-heterocyclic
compounds bearing an all-carbon quaternary stereogenic
center through the regio- and stereocontrolled functionaliza-
tion of allenes. This transformation not only expands the
synthetic utility of copper catalysis in constructing highly
congested stereocenters but also ofers a general and eficient
route to structurally diverse azaarene derivatives that may be of
value in drug discovery and related fields.

We further evaluated the applicability of this method to
other nitrogen-containing heterocycles. Isoquinoline, pyrazine,
and pyrimidine substrates all underwent the transformation
smoothly, afording the corresponding products 4q−4s in

contrast, the menthol-derived substrate delivered the product
4z in 60% yield with high enantioselectivity (95% ee).

insight into the reaction mechanism (Scheme 5). When

indicating that either the silane or copper hydride is involved in
the rate-determining step (Scheme 5b). Further initial rate
kinetic studies confirmed that both the copper and silane
contribute to the rate-determining step, supporting that copper
hydride generation is turnover-limiting (Scheme 5c).<sup>10,15</sup>

performed density functional theory (DFT) calculations. The
proposed mechanism involves a sequence of hydrocupration,

transition state, indicating its kinetic favorability. Although
halopyridines are known to engage in oxidative addition with
transition metals,<sup>8,16</sup> our calculations revealed that the
oxidative addition pathway involving 2-fluoropyridine has a
prohibitively high activation barrier of 59.7 kcal/mol from the

pathways involving (R)-Cu-2b and (S)-Cu-2b were excluded.

■ CONCLUSION
In summary, we have developed a copper-catalyzed enantio-
selective strategy for the construction of all-carbon quaternary
stereogenic centers adjacent to N-heterocycles via the
hydropyridylation of 1,1-disubstituted allenes. This trans-
formation proceeds under mild conditions with broad
functional group tolerance and delivers a wide array of N-
heterocycle-substituted products in high yields with excellent
enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee). The methodology was
further extended to copper-catalyzed boropyridylation, en-
abling access to synthetically versatile alkenylboronates that
can be readily transformed into ketones, alcohols, or
halogenated derivatives without erosion of the enantioselec-
tivity. Gram-scale synthesis and derivatizations�including
hydrogenation, hydroboration−oxidation, hydroformylation,
and hydroamination�underscore the robustness and synthetic
utility of this platform.
Mechanistic studies, including deuterium-labeling studies,
kinetic isotope efect measurements, and initial rate kinetic
experiments, indicate that copper hydride formation is
turnover-limiting. DFT calculations support a reaction pathway
involving regioselective 2,3-hydrocupration followed by a
stereodefining nucleophilic aromatic substitution
( S _ { \mathrm { { N } } } \mathbf { A r } )
step.
The origin of enantioselectivity is attributed to favorable non-
covalent interactions and minimized steric repulsion in the key
transition state. Together, these findings establish a robust
platform for the synthesis of highly congested azaarene
architectures and open new avenues for asymmetric catalysis
via nucleophilic aromatic substitution.
